brief: The Fed hiked 25bps to 3.75-4.0% on 17 September 2026, a unanimous vote and its first hike since 2023, reversing the easing cycle that had taken rates to a 3.75% trough in December 2025. SC attributes the hike to a summer pickup in job creation and inflation plus an oil-price rebound from re-escalation of the Middle East conflict, following Fed Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole warning. The unanimous vote, contrasting with July's 9-3 hold decision, signals Fed policymakers turned more hawkish and are rebuilding inflation-fighting credibility. SC expects one more hike by December and one more in H1 2027, on robust growth from AI investment and a tight labor market keeping inflation elevated, but that is fewer hikes than the three by June 2027 money markets are pricing. SC sees policy rates returning to the 4.0-4.25% range by end-2027, with possible cuts in H2 2027 as tariff and oil-price effects fade. SC raised its 3-month DXY target to 100 and its 3-month 10-year yield target to 5.0-5.25%.
